# Shared protocol profiles and repeatable verification

User explicitly requested design, implementation and deployment in this turn, without deferring the mechanism. This spec and plan supersede the old inline-only configuration design. Execute continuously in the existing isolated worktree on `codex/protocol-profiles`; use subagent-driven development where tool capacity permits. Preserve all existing permissions, supplier ordering, account cooldown, prices, billing fixes and streaming integrity.

## Design

One supplier/product profile is shared by account channels. The profile contains only nonsecret endpoint/policy data, never credentials. Channel keys, base URLs, proxies, model mapping, group abilities and account_resource stay on channels. Profiles cannot grant a model or group access. Match constraints (channel_types and base_urls) prevent accidental use on a different product; paths remain absolute paths on the existing host and retain current validation. Native protocol selection remains within the existing supplier/account order, and cross-format fidelity checks remain separate.

Configuration is backward compatible: existing inline settings keep their behavior. Add `profile` to ProtocolRoutingSettings. A selected profile permits empty local defaults, meaning inherit. Profile defaults and model differences are followed by channel defaults and channel model differences. A complete policy (nonempty entry_formats and endpoints) retains replacement semantics, including the historical safe default for omitted loss_policy. A partial policy inherits absent fields. Add `endpoint_overrides` to ProtocolModelPolicy: array of `{format, path?, features?: map<string,bool>, verified?: *bool, verified_at?: *string}`. Selectors match an existing endpoint; omitted path is valid only when exactly one endpoint has that format. True/false features add/remove; absent features inherit. This makes a model exception a few differences instead of a copied matrix. Resolved policies must pass existing full validation. No profile-to-profile inheritance or cycles.

Shared catalog is the existing options key `ProtocolProfiles`, JSON map profile ID to `{name, description?, channel_types?, base_urls?, defaults, models?}`. IDs are stable nonsecret `[a-z0-9_-]` names, at most64 bytes; at most32 profiles and60KiB encoded catalog. Profile defaults are complete, models may be partial. Publish immutable snapshots atomically, following RoutingPolicy rather than mutable reflection maps. Runtime resolves the selected model only, so template edits affect every reference without rewriting channels. Ordinary options synchronization propagates changes to other instances. API revision is a canonical SHA256 of the catalog; per-profile revision hashes support precise probe validity.

All catalog mutations and bulk bindings use the existing options/channel tables transactionally, the shared lockForUpdate helper, and optimistic revisions. No new tables, migrations, drivers or DB-specific SQL. In-use profiles cannot be removed; all bound channel overrides must still resolve when a profile is changed. Generic option update must not bypass these protections. Catalog and binding transactions lock the catalog row first. Bulk binding replaces duplicated protocol policy with a profile reference while preserving enabled/account_resource/quota_scope and every unrelated channel field. Detaching materializes the current effective policy. Preview before bulk changes; reject stale previews.

Unified tool classification recognizes ordinary functions/custom tools/namespaces and protocol-defined client tool families as client execution, and recognizes server-executed tools separately. Do not require hosted_tools merely because a client tool has a dated protocol type. Unknown classifications remain explicit in diagnostics rather than claiming a concrete provider is unsupported. Preserve stateful/background safeguards and cross-format loss checks. No blanket native passthrough of unknown billing parameters, no silent capability stripping, no invented supplier/model conditionals in application code.

## APIs and UI

Use `/api/channel/protocol/...` under existing AdminAuth plus channel permissions. Root is the current owner; no auth assurance is weakened. JSON writes use existing origin/CSRF protections where applicable, CriticalRateLimit and bounded request bodies. No keys, proxy credentials, headers or request/response content appear in API reports or errors.

- GET `/profiles`: ChannelRead. `{revision, profiles, channels}` where channel metadata is id/name/type/base_url/models/mapped_models/profile/enabled/account_resource, no keys or raw settings.
- PUT `/profiles`: ChannelWrite. `{revision, profiles}`; atomically validate/update entire catalog and existing bindings. Return current revision; stale changes409.
- POST `/bind`: ChannelWrite. `{revision, profile, channel_ids, preview}`. Profile empty means detach/materialize. Preview returns before/after effective policy summaries and an opaque binding fingerprint; apply requires that fingerprint. Preserve channel enable/identity and unrelated data.
- GET `/effective/:id`: ChannelRead. Resolved settings plus profile/revision/provenance, or canonical diagnostics.
- POST `/probes`: ChannelOperate. Create a persistent bounded report/plan for one profile: `{profile, channel_ids?, models?, formats?, checks, max_output_tokens?, allow_hosted?}`. Defaults choose representative bound channels per mapped model; explicit channel IDs can test all accounts. Native endpoints only, even currently unverified ones. Models must be advertised/mapped by selected channels. Max128 cases, max output1024(default256), response1MiB, per-case45s, concurrency2. Hosted web tests require explicit allow_hosted. No client-supplied prompts, headers, keys, external URLs or arbitrary tool code.
- GET `/probes` and GET `/probes/:id`: ChannelRead, persistent metadata/results, paginated/bounded. POST `/:id/run`: ChannelOperate, execute next bounded batch (2 cases concurrently, whole HTTP call≤60s) using request cancellation. UI drives successive batches; closing the page pauses work rather than leaving an unbounded background task. Reports persist completed cases. Atomically claim a batch, reject simultaneous runs, mark stale in-flight batches interrupted without silently retrying potentially consumed calls. POST `/:id/cancel`: ChannelOperate. Cancellation stops active local work and is persisted. Reports use existing option rows under `ProtocolProbeReport:` (not exported by GetOptions), bounded60KiB/report and last20 reports; never contain secrets or raw body content.
- POST `/probes/:id/apply`: ChannelWrite. Apply passed results only, preview changes first, require current catalog revision and unchanged relevant channel/profile fingerprints. Record applied revision idempotently. Reports store profile revision and HMAC fingerprints of relevant channel configuration/credentials; no credentials themselves. Failed/rejected/unknown outcomes never automatically remove a previously working capability. Generate minimal per-model endpoint_overrides, omitting changes already inherited; never change prices or group/model permissions.

Probe checks are shared fixtures: text(nonempty response), stream(valid content and terminal), tools(actual named function call and expected arguments), namespaces(Responses only, actual namespace preserved), images(synthetic solid-color PNG and correct color), web_search(actual completed search invocation/results, not declarations or HTTP200 alone). Mark passed/rejected/unknown/cancelled with canonical reason codes, HTTP status, terminal, reported usage, elapsed time and observed features. 429/5xx/timeouts/empty or truncated streams are unknown. 4xx rejection is only rejection of the fixture, not proof of permanent unsupported capability. Don't execute returned client tools. Keep transport/auth/header/proxy behavior in the relay layer using existing channel setup and redirect-safe DoApiRequest; probes do not touch team billing or channel health. Provider quota can be consumed, shown explicitly in UI.

UI reuses existing drawer sections, JsonCodeEditor, Select, shared dialogs/confirmation/table/loading/error components, React Query and seven-locale translation workflow. Channel form gets profile selection, inheritance help, effective preview, and local difference editors. A profile manager in channel management exposes editable templates, bindings, batch validation, progress/result matrix, JSON report export and preview/apply. Common cases do not require copying per-account JSON. No new UI library. Advanced JSON remains available for detailed policies; full and partial schema validation match backend.

## Verification and rollout

1. DTO/resolve tests protect inheritance order, explicit false removal, full legacy replacement, invalid/dangling selectors, reference failures and model isolation. Standalone relaykit GOWORK=off build required.
2. Real SQLite/MySQL/PostgreSQL exercise catalog CRUD, locking/revisions, references, atomic bindings/detach, reports and stale apply; no schema change is needed. Record exact engines/commands.
3. Synthetic local upstreams exercise all fixture verdicts, HTTP200 ignored tools, incomplete SSE, error results, reported usage, redirect refusal, cancellation, budgets, stale fingerprints and no credential/body leakage. New routes reject unauthorized/scope-insufficient callers; profile updates cannot bypass via generic options.
4. Frontend focused tests, full typecheck/lint/i18n/build; inspect UI in a real browser. Verify bulk workflow rather than implementation-only tests.
5. Complete app regression preserves existing native/cross paths, group order, all-account policy, tool accounting and stream errors. Independent final review.
6. Deploy versioned release with backups and request drain, following `.github/UPSTREAM_RELEASE_WORKFLOW.md`. Convert existing production inline data into supplier/product profiles plus minimal model exceptions, preserving effective behavior for every advertised mapped model. Snapshot only relevant metadata. Apply references only after all serving processes understand profiles. Use new batch workflow for bounded real representative validation; no automatic changes from transient probe failures. Preserve pricing/abilities/status hashes. Update existing runbook/verification/monitor and hourly automation as appropriate.

## Task ownership / contracts

Task1(parent): DTO partial-policy merge, shared immutable catalog and persistence, catalog/binding/effective APIs, runtime resolution and tool registry. Files relaykit/dto/protocol_routing.go; setting/protocol_setting; model/protocol_profiles.go +option/channel integration; service/protocol_policy.go; controller/protocol_profiles.go; router/channel-router.go. Exported contracts agreed before Task2/3 integration.
Task2(probe implementer): native bounded probe fixtures/transport/evidence + persistent batch plan/run/cancel/apply. Controller orchestrates relay and model; services must not import relay. Own controller/protocol_probes.go, relay/protocol_probe.go, service/protocol_probe.go, model/protocol_probe_reports.go, focused tests. Coordinate profile DTO and persistence helpers with Task1.
Task3(UI implementer): profile manager/channel binding/inheritance/probe UI, API/types/forms and seven locales. Own frontend only. Use endpoint contract above, request updates through parent if unavoidable.
Task4(parent + review): integrate, 3-DB matrix, complete app/browser verification, migrate/deploy/monitor, final documentation. One versioned release after combined verification; don't publish each small capability change separately.

Ruling: user has explicitly authorized design through implementation/deployment; skill review gates do not require repeated permission. Heartbeat read-only restrictions apply to the separate monitoring action, not this explicitly authorized development. Reuse the existing isolated checkout; preserve completed earlier fixes. If fresh-agent capacity is unavailable, record it and reuse available agents or execute locally rather than stalling.
